old:
Let $\tilde k_{s}$ and $\tilde k_{s}^{\sharp}$ be $C^{1,1}$ diffeomorphisms of $S^{1}$ with
$\tilde k_{s}|_{I}=\tilde k_{s}^{\sharp}|_{I}=k_{s}$, and let $U_{s},U_{s}^{\sharp}$ be implementers as in
\Cref{H1}.  Then $\omega\circ\Ad U_{s}|_{\cM}=\omega\circ\Ad U_{s}^{\sharp}|_{\cM}$.
new:
Let $g_{\rm tot}$ and $g_{\rm tot}^{\sharp}$ be two first-order fields in the extension class $\mathcal E$ of
\cite[Def.~2.1]{RigorC} (real, $C^{1}$ on $S^{1}$, $C^{\infty}$ off the touching point, $0$ on $A$ and equal to
the M\"obius field $m$ on $D$; \eqref{eq:chi} is one of them), so that their flows $\tilde k_{s}$,
$\tilde k_{s}^{\sharp}$ both restrict to $k_{s}$ on $I$, and let $U_{s}=e^{is\overline{T(g_{\rm tot})}}$ and
$U_{s}^{\sharp}=e^{is\overline{T(g^{\sharp}_{\rm tot})}}$ be the implementers of \Cref{thm:H1}.  Then
$\omega\circ\Ad U_{s}|_{\cM}=\omega\circ\Ad U_{s}^{\sharp}|_{\cM}$ for every $s\ge0$.
reason: restates lem:ext in the form implementation_C11.tex Thm 4.7 step <1>7 proves (class E, s >= 0); the old statement (arbitrary C^{1,1} extensions, both signs of s) is unproved.

old:
Put $\phi:=\tilde k_{s}\circ(\tilde k_{s}^{\sharp})^{-1}$ and $J_{s}:=k_{s}(I)$.  For $y\in J_{s}$ write
$y=k_{s}(x)$ with $x\in I$; then $(\tilde k^{\sharp}_{s})^{-1}(y)=x$ and $\tilde k_{s}(x)=k_{s}(x)=y$, so
$\phi|_{J_{s}}=\mathrm{id}$, i.e.\ $\phi\in\mathrm{Diff}(J_{s}')$.  By the locality clause
\eqref{eq:H1loc} with $K=J_{s}'$ we get $U(\phi)\in\cA(J_{s}')$, and hence $U(\phi)\in\cA(J_{s})'$ by
\emph{locality} alone.  Now let $X\in\cM$.  By covariance, $Y:=U^{\sharp}_{s}XU_{s}^{\sharp*}\in
\cA(\tilde k^{\sharp}_{s}(I))=\cA(J_{s})$, so $U(\phi)YU(\phi)^{*}=Y$.  Since $U_{s}$ and
$U(\phi)U^{\sharp}_{s}$ implement the same diffeomorphism they agree up to a phase $\lambda$, $|\lambda|=1$,
which cancels in $\Ad$; therefore
$U_{s}XU_{s}^{*}=U(\phi)YU(\phi)^{*}=Y=U^{\sharp}_{s}XU_{s}^{\sharp*}$, and applying $\omega$ finishes the
proof.
\end{proof}

Note that $\phi$ is in general supported on the \emph{closed} arc $\overline{J_s'}$, which is why
\eqref{eq:H1loc} rather than a support condition is the right hypothesis.
new:
This is \cite[Thm.~4.7, step $\langle1\rangle7$]{RigorC}; we give the argument.  Put
$f:=g_{\rm tot}-g^{\sharp}_{\rm tot}$.  It is real, $\|f\|_{3/2}<\infty$ (\cite[Thm.~2.3(c)]{RigorC}, which holds on
all of $\mathcal E$), and $f=0$ on the open interval $I$, so $V_{t}:=e^{it\overline{T(f)}}\in\cA(I)'=\cM'$ for all
$t$ by \Cref{lem:loc}(i).  Let $X\in\cM$ and $a\ge0$.  By \Cref{thm:H1}(iii) for $g^{\sharp}_{\rm tot}$ (\cite[Thm.~4.7]{RigorC} proves it on all of $\mathcal E$),
$\Ad U^{\sharp}_{a}(X)\in\cA(\tilde k^{\sharp}_{a}I)$, and $\tilde k^{\sharp}_{a}I=k_{a}(I)\subseteq I$ because
$a\ge0$ moves the far endpoint of $I$ inwards; so $\Ad U^{\sharp}_{a}(X)\in\cM$ commutes with $V_{a}$ and
$\Ad(V_{a}U^{\sharp}_{a})(X)=\Ad U^{\sharp}_{a}(X)\in\cM$.  By induction on $n$,
$\Ad\bigl((V_{s/n}U^{\sharp}_{s/n})^{n}\bigr)(X)=\Ad U^{\sharp}_{s}(X)$ for $s\ge0$.  On the common core
$\Hil_{\rm fin}$ one has $T(g_{\rm tot})=T(f)+T(g^{\sharp}_{\rm tot})$ term by term, and $T(g_{\rm tot})$ is
essentially self-adjoint there \cite[Thm.~4.4]{CW}; so $\overline{T(f)}+\overline{T(g^{\sharp}_{\rm tot})}$, a
symmetric extension of it, is essentially self-adjoint with closure $\overline{T(g_{\rm tot})}$, and the
Trotter product formula (Reed--Simon Thm.~VIII.31, as in \Cref{thm:H1}) gives
$(V_{s/n}U^{\sharp}_{s/n})^{n}\to U_{s}$ strongly.  Strong convergence of unitaries implies that of their
adjoints, hence $\Ad\bigl((V_{s/n}U^{\sharp}_{s/n})^{n}\bigr)(X)\to\Ad U_{s}(X)$ strongly, so
$\Ad U_{s}(X)=\Ad U^{\sharp}_{s}(X)$, and applying $\omega$ finishes the proof.
\end{proof}

The restrictions $s\ge0$ and $\mathcal E$ are those of the proof: for $s<0$ the arc $\tilde k_{s}I$ is not
contained in $I$, and for a $C^{1,1}$ extension outside $\mathcal E$ no implementer statement is proved here.
An earlier version of this lemma applied \eqref{eq:H1loc} to $\phi=\tilde k_{s}\circ(\tilde k_{s}^{\sharp})^{-1}$,
which is only $C^{1,1}$, so that $U(\phi)$ is not defined; that argument is withdrawn.  \Cref{thm:B} does not
use \Cref{lem:ext}.
reason: the old proof applied eq:H1loc to the C^{1,1} map phi, for which U(phi) is not defined; the new proof uses only lem:loc(i), thm:H1(iii) and Trotter, as C11 <1>7 does.

new:
Let $\cA_{1},\cA_{2}$ satisfy the hypotheses of \Cref{thm:B}, with central charges $c_{1},c_{2}$, and assume
that $\cA=\cA_{1}\otimes\cA_{2}$ does too.  Then $f_{2}(\cA)=f_{2}(\cA_{1})+f_{2}(\cA_{2})$.  Indeed the stress
tensor of $\cA$ is $T(f)=T_{1}(f)\otimes\one+\one\otimes T_{2}(f)$, so its central charge is $c=c_{1}+c_{2}$,
and \Cref{thm:B} applied to each of the three nets gives $f_{2}=c/(12\pi^{2})$, which is additive in $c$.

$\overline{\cM'_{\rm sa}\Omega}$, not a norm.)
